ITS.journal: One row per journal. Holds the journal's identity (title, short code/abbreviation, ISSN/DOI), lifecycle flags (active/visible/published status — several separate flags, each tracking a DIFFERENT thing, see column descriptions), access type (subscription vs open access), and metrics (impact factor, rankings). Does NOT store editor/people information directly — eic_detail and eic_detail_old are always empty. To find WHO holds any editorial role (including Editor-in-Chief) for a journal, join to ITS.tbl_ebm on journal_id, then to ITS.tbl_ebm_role (to filter/identify the specific role by name) and ITS.tbl_editors (to get that person's actual name/contact details). A journal's short code/abbreviation may appear in more than one column (e.g. jms_jcode and abbrev_journal_title_dummy) — check multiple short-code columns, or use find_value_anywhere, rather than assuming only one holds it.
ITS.tbl_ebm: One row per (editor, role, journal) assignment — i.e. one editor holding one specific editorial role on one specific journal. This is the join table connecting people (ITS.tbl_editors) to journals (ITS.journal) to roles (ITS.tbl_ebm_role). Any question that combines a PERSON with a ROLE with a JOURNAL (e.g. 'who is the EIC of journal X', 'how many regional editors does journal Y have', 'which journals does editor Z work on') needs this table as the join hub: journal_id -> ITS.journal, editor_id -> ITS.tbl_editors, role_id (or ebm_role_id, a duplicate) -> ITS.tbl_ebm_role. ebm_status ('Active'/'Resigned') indicates whether the assignment currently holds — filter to ebm_status = 'Active' unless the question is specifically about historical/resigned appointments.
ITS.tbl_ebm_role: A small, fixed lookup table of editorial role DEFINITIONS — NOT a per-editor or per-journal table. One row per distinct role type (Editor-in-Chief, Co-Editor-in-Chief, Regional Editor, Section Editor, etc. — there are multiple roles, not just one). Both 'role' (short form) and 'nicename' (full form) name the same role — check whichever matches the user's own wording more closely; do not assume the user's phrasing must match one specific form. To find WHO holds a given role, this table alone is not enough — join to ITS.tbl_ebm on role_id (or ebm_role_id) to see which editors/journals that role is actually assigned to.
ITS.tbl_editors: One row per editor/person, with their name, degrees, affiliation (university/institute/department), contact info, and academic identifiers (ORCID, Scopus ID, etc.). Does NOT store which journal(s) or role(s) an editor holds — that's in ITS.tbl_ebm (join on editor_id). status tracks the editor's account status (active/blocked/deleted), which is separate from ebm_status on tbl_ebm (which tracks whether a specific role assignment is active/resigned) — a blocked editor account and a resigned role assignment are different, independently-tracked facts.
